claims.title: Exact finite rational observation-channel coding game
claims.scope: finite rational source-law scenarios, a finite public rational observation channel, and a complete bounded deterministic zero-error prefix-code universe
assumptions: nature selects one declared source-law scenario
the public signal follows the declared row-stochastic channel conditional on that scenario
policy, code, dominance, and game support enumerations complete below configured caps
nonclaims: the finite scenario set is not a continuum or statistical coverage theorem
the observation channel is assumed known rather than estimated

claims.title: Public randomization value is distinct from source-law information value
claims.scope: the declared deterministic and shared-randomness no-signal and signal-policy minimax values
assumptions: the public signal and any shared seed are known to every decoder
shared randomization is independent of the source-law scenario
cost is expected zero-error prefix length
nonclaims: an uninformative random signal can coordinate actions without revealing the scenario
deterministic observation and shared no-signal resources are not generally totally ordered

claims.title: Blackwell garbling monotonicity for shared-randomness coding value
claims.scope: two finite rational observation channels where the second equals the first composed with a declared row-stochastic garbling kernel
assumptions: the designer may use public shared randomness independent of the source scenario
both channels are evaluated on the same source-law scenarios, code universe, and loss
nonclaims: the theorem is stated for the shared-randomness value because simulating a stochastic garbling requires admitted randomness
Blackwell order is a partial order and is not replaced by one scalar information score

claims.title: Exact sensing-cost threshold equals incremental information value
claims.scope: one optional observation-channel use compared with the shared-randomness no-signal baseline
assumptions: the sensing charge is a nonnegative declared additive cost
the channel-assisted and baseline coding games use the same source scenarios and code universe
nonclaims: the sensing charge is not inferred from physical measurement cost
the tie-breaking convention declines sensing at exact equality

claims.title: Half-accurate symmetric K3 observation has exact seven-over-sixty information value
claims.scope: complete three-state confusion graph, three heavy-state source scenarios with mass 4/5, and symmetric signal accuracy 1/2
nonclaims: the exact fractions are specific to the declared K3 instance
classification accuracy alone is not asserted sufficient to rank arbitrary channels

claims.title: Bounded exact observation-policy and Blackwell audit
claims.scope: the rational channels, deterministic policies, game supports, garblings, and sensing decisions exercised by the repository tests
assumptions: all configured policy, dominance, code, and game support caps complete without truncation
Python Fraction arithmetic is used for all channel and payoff calculations
nonclaims: CI success is not a large-instance or continuous-observation theorem
finite decision-value calculations are not evidence that reality is simulated
